races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF (C & G) Maiden
Bahrain Turf Club Desmond Stakes (Group 3)

runners_data.name: Audience
runners_data.note: Hold-up style seven-year-old whose recent form shows consistent place-getting without winning (0W3P on similar going); Colin Keane provides tactical awareness but the form string of 000923 suggests a horse that arrives in frame rather than wins, and the step up from seven furlongs to a mile here is a query given its recent route preference.
runners_data.comment: Placed on each of his last two starts — third most recently, second two back — Audience has run over today's trip and going, and his rating of 117 puts him top of the field on our figures; yet to score in recent starts, but the consistency and 18-day turnaround make him the one to side with.

runners_data.name: Chicago Critic
runners_data.note: Hold-up five-year-old with solid but uninspiring place form across this distance range (1W3P on similar going); Ben Coen is a quality booking for JP Murtagh's yard, but 40 days off and a tendency to run into positions rather than win means it needs a very strongly run race to land the blow.
runners_data.comment: Chicago Critic has run over today's trip and going, rates 7 lb above his official mark on our figures, and 40 days between runs leaves him fresh enough to improve — the risk is that he's been winless in his last six starts, those three fourths suggesting he finds one or two too good.

runners_data.name: Cowardofthecounty
runners_data.note: Joseph Patrick O'Brien four-year-old with genuine hold-up tendencies that will place it further back than the map indicates — its recent 1-2-3 run of form over seven and eight furlongs on Good-to-Soft is encouraging, but racing in traffic off a slow pace on this map position understates how far back it will actually sit, tempering its winning chance here.
runners_data.comment: Cowardofthecounty arrives with solid recent form — a winner three starts back, third two starts back, and second last time out — keeping good company on the whole, and he has experience of today's distance and going. The main risk is whether his speed rating of 94 can match the very best here.

runners_data.name: Tokenomics
runners_data.note: Prominent five-year-old with three wins from 15 runs on similar going and solid each-way profile over this mile trip; Luke McAteer takes over and the horse's front-rank cruising style suits a contested pace scenario where it can track the leaders and attack in the straight without expending early energy.
runners_data.comment: Tokenomics showed a second two starts back but has since disappointed with a sixth last time out, and the 39-day absence adds a fitness query; he has run over today's trip and going, and carries 135 lb from stall nine.

runners_data.name: Celtic Motif
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for O'Brien returning off 23 days, with a win last time out over this course and distance on Good ground (1W4P on similar going) giving real claims; the risk is that Needle Match will contest the lead directly and Celtic Motif may lack the reserves to repel a quality field if it burns itself out early.
runners_data.comment: Celtic Motif won last time out and has run over today's trip and going, but she ranks eighth of nine on our figures with a speed rating of 76, making her hard to fancy at this level despite the recent winning form.

runners_data.name: Al Haarith
runners_data.note: Three-year-old prominent racer with the highest OR in the field (106) and a course win last time out on Good ground, ridden by the in-form Dylan Browne McMonagle for the powerful O'Brien yard; the 1W2P record on similar going and youth allied to class makes this the standout beneficiary of the contested pace scenario, tracking the leaders from a compact position.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of nine on our figures, Al Haarith faces a stiff ask, and his patchy recent form — unplaced second time back before winning last time out — offers mixed signals. He has run over today's trip and returns on a handy 26-day break, but the rating gap is hard to overlook.

runners_data.name: Isaac Newton
runners_data.note: Hold-up three-year-old ridden by Ryan Moore dropping back from longer trips (9-12 furlongs recently) to a mile, which is a genuine query — his one win this season came over nine furlongs; the class of Moore and A P O'Brien is always live, but the trip contraction needs to be proven.
runners_data.comment: A winner three starts back but sixth two starts back and only third last time out, Isaac Newton arrives with patchy recent form that makes him hard to fancy ranked seventh of nine. He has run over today's distance and going, and 21 days between runs suggests he's ready.

runners_data.name: Needle Match
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for William Haggas returning off a lengthy 96-day break after finishing fourth at Royal Ascot; the freshener could sharpen it but also introduces a fitness question, and Tom Marquand will need to judge the pace battle with Celtic Motif carefully to avoid a suicidal early duel that benefits the holds-up horses.
runners_data.comment: Needle Match landed a win three starts back but has since gone unplaced, and 96 days off the track raises fitness questions; he has run over today's trip and going, and carries 128 lb from stall six.

runners_data.name: Sparan Nua
runners_data.note: Unexposed three-year-old dropping sharply from 10-12 furlongs to a mile on the back of three wins (3W4P on similar going) trained by Jim Bolger; Declan McDonogh knows the horse well, but the trip contraction is significant and it is unknown whether the shorter, sharper pace of a Desmond Stakes will suit this staying profile.
runners_data.comment: Sparan Nua arrives in cracking form, winning three of her last four starts, and she has experience of today's trip and conditions — the main question is whether that third last time out signals any vulnerability at the top of the weights carrying 128 lb.

races.paceDynamic: Needle Match and Celtic Motif are both confirmed front-runners in a nine-runner field, setting up a directly contested early pace that should produce an honest, even gallop from the off rather than a dawdle. With two horses fighting for the lead through Leopardstown's opening bend, neither is likely to dominate entirely, and the resulting pace should be genuine enough to stretch the field before the home turn. Cowardofthecounty is a true hold-up type who has been redistributed to midfield on the map because this field contains more deep closers than can all occupy the rear — in reality it will likely settle further back than its mapped position suggests, and the hold-up runners behind it will be similarly compressed. This race shape — genuine front-running pace from two identifiable leaders, Good ground, and a one-mile trip — favours prominent racers who can track the duel and pounce in the straight, particularly those with proven tactical speed over this distance on similar ground.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Needle Match and Celtic Motif fight for supremacy and set an honest gallop, allowing a well-positioned prominent horse to travel smoothly and strike decisively entering the final furlong.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners burn each other off through a genuine early pace, leaving the race wide open for a horse tracking just behind who has conserved energy through the middle stages; on Good Leopardstown turf over a mile, this is the optimal scenario for a quality prominent racer with tactical speed.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Survives Duel
scenarios.trigger: If one front-runner, most likely Needle Match, asserts dominance early and gets an uncontested or semi-uncontested lead, rationing effort through the middle and holding on gamely.
scenarios.body: Celtic Motif's lesser class at this level may see it fade after the initial tussle, leaving Needle Match in front on its own terms with sufficient gallop reserves to repel challengers in the straight; William Haggas's colt showed winning speed on debut and has been freshened by a 96-day break, which could mean it returns sharper.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runners set a genuinely strong pace that tests the prominent horses, allowing deep closers to sweep through late with a sustained finishing effort.
scenarios.body: Isaac Newton and Audience have the tactical capacity to come from off the pace, and a hot early gallop would play directly to their preference for a strongly run race; Ryan Moore aboard Isaac Newton is a significant asset in a scenario that demands late-race positioning and timing.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Sprint Finish
scenarios.trigger: If neither front-runner fully commits and the early gallop proves deceptive, producing a compressed field and a sprint from two furlongs out.
scenarios.body: A falsely-run mile on Good ground can catch hold-up horses flat-footed while a sharp, adaptable prominent type with a high cruising speed wins the sprint; this scenario is less likely given two genuine front-runners are declared, but remains a residual risk if early race tactics change.

watchPoints.text: Needle Match and Celtic Motif — watch the first two furlongs closely; if both commit aggressively to the lead, the resulting hot pace dramatically increases the chance of a prominent or hold-up horse winning and shortens the odds of either front-runner lasting home.

Isaac Newton — Ryan Moore dropping a three-year-old back from trips of nine furlongs and beyond to a flat mile is a notable step; if the horse is seen to travel without fluency or comes off the bridle early, the trip contraction has found it out.

Sparan Nua — Bolger's three-year-old arrives on a winning streak but has only run over 10-12 furlongs; watch how it settles behind the pace in the early stages, as any sign of pulling or racing keenly would be a negative given the shorter, sharper demands of this race.

Al Haarith — the O'Brien yard sends out three runners (Al Haarith, Celtic Motif, Cowardofthecounty) and team tactics may influence how Celtic Motif is ridden early; if the pacemaker role is sacrificed, Al Haarith's prominent position becomes even more powerful.

Cowardofthecounty — watch where Ronan Whelan actually positions this horse at the start; despite being shown in midfield on the map, its natural instinct is to drop away to the rear, and if it settles in the back third it will need a stronger pace than may materialise to produce its finishing effort in time.

races.name: Ballyroan Stakes (Group 3)

runners_data.name: Ascending
runners_data.note: A seven-year-old who won over 20f on Good last time out and has strong course-and-distance form; a natural prominent racer who will likely find himself in a deeper position than ideal given the crowded pace map, which tempers his winning chance in a shape that rewards true prominent horses.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of nine on our figures and beaten in his last three starts, Ascending is hard to fancy despite carrying a manageable 135 lb; he has run over today's trip and going before, and a win and second in recent starts show he can perform when conditions click.

runners_data.name: Dallas Star
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who will go straight to the front, but his recent form string of 332547 shows he has been placed rather than winning, and he steps up in company here; his role is likely pace-setter for others rather than winner.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Dallas Star has at least shown consistency at this level, finishing second and third in recent starts, though seventh last time out after 47 days off is a concern; he has experience of today's trip and going, but his rating suggests he faces a stiff task from the middle of the field.

runners_data.name: Ethical Diamond
runners_data.note: The highest-rated runner at OR 118 with Ryan Moore aboard and W P Mullins training; three wins at 12f on Good ground and a class edge over most rivals make him the standout candidate if he settles just off the contested lead, which is his natural position.|
runners_data.comment: Ethical Diamond landed back-to-back wins three and four starts back and a further success five starts back, showing real consistency at the top level; he has experience over today's trip and going, and 135 lb is the primary concern after 47 days off.

runners_data.name: Gaucher
runners_data.note: A Mullins stablemate of Ethical Diamond who won at 12f on Standard and has not raced beyond 10f on Good ground; the switch to Good turf at 1m4f is a legitimate query, and he will need to settle in a prominent position to be at his best.|
runners_data.comment: Gaucher brings strong recent form to this contest — a winner three starts back and second two starts back show he fires in this sphere, and experience over today's trip and going is a plus; the 51-day absence is the one concern.

runners_data.name: Green Impact
runners_data.note: Shane Foley rides a four-year-old who is 3W from 4P on Good going but has not won beyond 9f in that sphere; the step up to 1m4f is the key question, and prominent placement will be needed given the pace congestion ahead of him.|

runners_data.name: Layfayette
runners_data.note: At nine, Colin Keane's mount has two wins from 12f and 14f in the last five, including on Soft; the sole genuine hold-up type in the field, he will benefit most if the contested front-running produces a strong, true gallop that rewards one late run.|
runners_data.comment: Layfayette arrives here in fine fettle, a winner last time out and second two starts back, showing consistent form at the top of the weights on 135 lb; he has experience over today's trip and going, and a 48-day break shouldn't blunt his edge.

runners_data.name: Omni Man
runners_data.note: Joseph O'Brien's four-year-old holds a prominent profile by nature but the crowded pace map means he is likely to race further back than he would prefer; his recent form shows multiple missed placings, and racing out of role further reduces his appeal here.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked seventh of nine on our figures, Omni Man faces a stiff ask here; a third four starts back offers some hope, but recent efforts of fifth, eighth and ninth make him hard to fancy, despite experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Asakir
runners_data.note: Ben Coen's three-year-old is the younger and lighter of the two front-runners at 125lbs; he won at 10f on Soft and was placed at 13f and 14f, showing the trip is fine, but his Good-ground sim stats are thin and contested pace with an older rival is a stern test.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked eighth of nine on our figures, Asakir's recent form reads poorly after finishing seventh last time out, and he has been off the track for 50 days; the one bright spot is a win three starts back, and he does have experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Endorsement
runners_data.note: Dylan Browne McMonagle partners this lightly raced three-year-old who has been placed in five of his last five and won at 12f on Soft; he wants a prominent position and his consistency at 10-12f suggests the 14f on Good is a slight unknown, but he is upwardly mobile and worth respect.|
runners_data.comment: Ran well enough last time when second, and a winner two starts back, but the 49-day break is a query for a colt who must give weight all round; he has run over today's trip and going, though, which at least removes one unknown.

races.paceDynamic: Dallas Star and Asakir are both confirmed front-runners and will contest the lead from the off over this 1m4f trip on Good ground, creating a genuine, honest gallop rather than a falsely run affair. Behind them, Ethical Diamond, Gaucher, Green Impact, and Endorsement all want prominent positions, generating meaningful congestion in the first few furlongs that could produce shuffling and interference two to three furlongs out. Layfayette, the sole genuine hold-up horse, will settle deepest and look for one sustained run from the home turn. This field contains more prominent-leaning types than the race shape can accommodate cleanly — Dallas Star and Asakir are most likely to actually secure their front-running positions, while Omni Man and Ascending, though natural prominent racers, will find themselves shuffled back into midfield roles they do not truly suit. The contested early fractions and honest gallop favour a horse that can travel prominently without burning fuel, then sustain a finish — making the patient but prominent profile the primary beneficiary of this race shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Lead, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Dallas Star and Asakir trade blows in front at an honest clip, setting it up for a prominent stalker to strike turning in.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners burn each other off across 1m4f on Good ground, leaving the first pursuit group ideally placed to pounce entering the straight; a horse who has tracked the pace within two lengths without expending early energy owns the finish.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Kicks Clear
scenarios.trigger: If one of the two pace-setters establishes a clear lead, soft-pedals the middle section, and finds enough fuel to resist late challengers.
scenarios.body: A lulled middle portion means the lead horse conserves energy and opens up again in the straight before the prominent horses can close; the contested nature makes this less likely but the Good ground and 1m4f trip give a class front-runner a chance to steal it.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the contested early pace is genuinely strong enough to string the field out and create significant daylight for a late finisher.
scenarios.body: Layfayette, the only true hold-up type, gets a clean passage down the outside and delivers one sustained run from two furlongs out as the pace-compromised horses in front tire; this shape requires both front-runners to truly go hard, which is plausible but not guaranteed.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Midfield Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If the two front-runners sense each other and both ease off, creating a falsely run race that bunches the field approaching the final turn.
scenarios.body: Congestion throughout the race erupts into a sprint finish for which the horse with the best acceleration from a midfield position wins; however, neither Dallas Star nor Asakir has the profile to suddenly become a dawdler, making this the least likely shape.

watchPoints.text: Dallas Star and Asakir will both press for the early lead — watch for a sharp duel in the opening two furlongs that could compromise both their finishing efforts and create a falsely collapsed pace if one blinks early.

Prominent congestion involving Ethical Diamond, Gaucher, Green Impact, and Endorsement directly behind the pace means serious traffic risk two to three furlongs out — any horse caught wide or pocketed at that point is in danger of losing its race before the straight begins.

Omni Man and Ascending are natural prominent horses mapped to midfield by force — if either rider pushes forward to reclaim their natural position, it adds to the early congestion and could make the pace even hotter than anticipated.

Layfayette at nine years old has won over this type of trip and going but his Good-ground sim record shows no wins in ten attempts at the meeting level — his hold-up run is the natural late threat but his record on this surface deserves scrutiny.

Ethical Diamond steps back up from 12f having finished ninth last time out — Ryan Moore will look to slot in just behind the pace and that recovery run at a longer trip for a horse with three wins at 12f and one at 14f on Good is worth tracking from the outset.

races.name: Carnival de Leop Handicap

runners_data.name: Dinamine
runners_data.note: True hold-up type returning in fair form (finished 1st and 3rd in last five on similar going), Wesley Joyce claiming 3lb is a useful allowance in a competitive handicap — needs a clear run in a 20-horse field to produce his best.|
runners_data.comment: Dinamine won last time out and has run over today's trip and going before, so he arrives with some relevant experience; however, he was fifth one start back and has shown inconsistency in recent starts, and a rating of 57 gives him little margin over the field.

runners_data.name: Imperial Dream
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer at OR=59 but recent form shows worrying strings of zeros on Good and Standard ground; Alan Persse's 5lb claim is attractive but the form line gives little confidence.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Imperial Dream nonetheless catches the eye on ratings — our figure of 68 ranks him second of 19 — and he has run over today's trip and going before, carrying 142 lb from stall 2 on a quick 19-day turnaround; the risk is that recent form has been consistently disappointing.

runners_data.name: Pete's Dream
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner, rated just 59 and dropping back in quality, but his ability to set a solo uncontested lead at his own pace is his biggest asset — STYLE_FIT flag notes he may be racing somewhat out of role at this trip, so the easy lead is his main chance.|
runners_data.comment: Pete's Dream arrives on the back of a win one start back and ran third last time out, showing improved recent form; he has experience of today's trip and conditions, and 22 days since his last run leaves him fresh — the main risk is whether 142 lb from stall one ultimately takes its toll late on.

runners_data.name: Wellwhatshappenin
runners_data.note: Returns from 139-day absence with a fade-in-finish flag and no Leopardstown form in the recent record; the Harty yard's 0/4 T14 suggests the stable is not currently firing and a first-time run back after such a break adds risk.|
runners_data.comment: Showed a win and placed efforts earlier in his recent sequence, but unplaced last time and returns after 139 days off; has run over today's trip and carries 141 lb from stall 9, though a rating of 56 leaves him with ground to find on the top runners.

runners_data.name: The Blue Panther
runners_data.note: Strong recent run to finish second on Good ground at 7f is directly relevant here; Nicola Burns's 5lb claim helps with the weight, though an 8-year-old's ability to reproduce that consistently is a key caveat.|
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in his last five starts, The Blue Panther bounces back quickly on 12 days' rest and has experience of today's trip and going — his second last time out offers encouragement, though 140 lb from stall 20 may not help his cause.

runners_data.name: Brains
runners_data.note: Prominent type with solid place consistency including a second on Good ground in recent starts; Sam Coen's 5lb claim is a live factor and 7f on Good suits, though the age (10) and tongue-tie must be noted.|
runners_data.comment: Brains arrives here fit on a 12-day turnaround, has run over today's trip and going, and our rating of 64 puts him comfortably clear of his official mark — a second four starts back hints at better days; the concern is he's been winless in his last six starts.

runners_data.name: Gordon Bennett
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type making his return from 246 days off, which is a major concern in a competitive field; all recent form is at 6f on Standard/Heathfield ground, making the 7f Leopardstown trip a step into the unknown.|
runners_data.comment: Gordon Bennett returns after 246 days off the track, and while he's winless in recent starts, that third one start back shows he retains ability; our rating of 69 heads the field, and experience over today's trip and going underlines his claims from stall 15.

runners_data.name: Launch Time
runners_data.note: Prominent runner for Colin Keane — the jockey upgrade is significant — with a win at 8f on Good ground showing he stays well; dropping in distance to 7f could sharpen his finishing kick if the pace is honest.|
runners_data.comment: Third last time out offers encouragement, but a ninth the start before is harder to overlook — Launch Time has run over today's trip and returns after a 36-day break carrying 136 lb from stall 16, leaving him with plenty to do from a midfield ranking.

runners_data.name: Dress Dance
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse whose natural rear position has been redistributed to midfield given the density of closers in this field; fades in finish flag and four zeros in recent form make her a tough sell on current form regardless of where she sits.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts and off the track for 79 days, Dress Dance faces a stiff ask from 135 lb, though she has run over today's trip before and draw three gives her a straightforward enough pitch from which to show more.

runners_data.name: Micasso
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up performer with a recent win on Good going and tongue-tie in place — his real style means he'll push to get closer to the pace than the map shows; the OR=52 looks workable if he secures a handy pitch.|
runners_data.comment: Unplaced last time out and rated well below the field on our figures, Micasso is hard to fancy despite that win one start back; he has run over today's trip and returns after 25 days, but stall 14 and 135 lb make this a tough ask.

runners_data.name: Jazzit
runners_data.note: Primarily a hold-up type whose recent form is all at 5-6f and switching up to 7f here; jockey Sadhbh Tormey is a 7lb claimer, which assists the weight, but the step in trip and loss of natural position make this a difficult assignment.|
runners_data.comment: Jazzit showed up with a third last time out and a third six starts back, but those eighths two and three starts back are a concern; he has run over today's distance and going, yet winless in his last six, he faces a stiff task from stall 8 off 133 lb.

runners_data.name: Cordouan
runners_data.note: A fade-in-finish flag combined with four finishes of 8th or worse in recent starts on similar going signals a horse who is struggling to compete at this level; redistribution from hold-up to midfield further compromises his best running style.|

runners_data.name: Mogwli
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old hold-up type mapped to midfield through redistribution, with a string of zeros in recent form and all recent runs in double-figure positions — difficult to make a case for him in this competitive 20-runner field.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and absent for 86 days, Mogwli faces a stiff task from stall 17 carrying 130 lb, though he has run over today's trip and going before and our rating of 63 suggests more ability than his official mark of 47 implies.

runners_data.name: Pure Valour
runners_data.note: Lightly-raced four-year-old with only four runs visible and no win or place on Good ground; redistribution away from his preferred hold-up spot makes this a challenging race shape to navigate for a horse still learning his trade.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts with finishes of ninth, seventh, sixth and unplaced, Pure Valour heads into this from stall 18 carrying 130 lb and ranks near the foot of our figures — experience over today's trip is the one box she ticks.

runners_data.name: Smaoineamh Sile
runners_data.note: Fade-in-finish flag and an unseated rider in recent form create serious questions; the true hold-up style has been pushed into midfield by the redistribution, compounding the tactical challenge for Robert Whearty.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts — including an unseating two back and a ninth most recently — Smaoineamh Sile faces an uphill task, though she has run over today's trip and going before and returns fit enough on 21 days' rest.

runners_data.name: Cannonball Queen
runners_data.note: Four-year-old filly with a row of zeros on Good ground at 7f — the form could hardly be more discouraging — and the fade-in-finish flag suggests she finds little when it matters; the redistribution away from her natural position is a further headache.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and off the track for 94 days, Cannonball Queen faces a stiff task ranked 16 of 19 on our figures; she has run over today's trip before, and stall seven is her draw, but it's hard to build a case from a sequence of five unplaced efforts.

runners_data.name: Draiocht
runners_data.note: Fade-in-finish flag and a hood, having won once on Soft ground, with the redistribution from hold-up to midfield meaning Wayne Lordan will be managing an awkward positional compromise in a 20-runner field.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked 18 of 19 on our figures, Draiocht has managed just one win in his last five starts with two notably poor efforts sandwiching that success; he has run over today's trip and going, but from stall 19 carrying 126 lb, there is precious little here to inspire confidence.

runners_data.name: Master Garvey
runners_data.note: All recent runs have been at 8-10f on Good ground and the drop to 7f is a significant unknown; the redistribution to midfield from his true hold-up style means Terry Casey faces a difficult tactical puzzle with a horse that has been running longer distances.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Master Garvey ranks 15th of 19 on our figures and carries 123 lb from stall 12, making him hard to fancy; a third last time out offers a crumb of hope, and he has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Desert Of The Sea
runners_data.note: Prominent type drawn in an exposed position in a large field, with James Ryan riding — recent form shows consistent mid-pack finishes at 7-9f on Good/Standard, and a low OR of 38 means the weight is in his favour if the race develops cleanly.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and ranked last on our figures, Desert Of The Sea faces a stiff ask here; three modest efforts since a brief purple patch of placed finishes are hard to ignore, though he has run over today's trip and going before and returns on a fresh enough 35-day break.

runners_data.name: Suerte
runners_data.note: Having run just three days ago, the extremely short turnaround to this race is a significant red flag regardless of ability; hold-up type on Good ground at 7f, with W J Lee up, but the fresh-from-race concern is the dominant note here.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and back up just three days after her latest unplaced effort, Suerte faces a stiff ask, though she has run over today's trip and going before and our rating nudges above her official mark, offering a sliver of encouragement from stall 10 at 139 lb.

races.paceDynamic: Pete's Dream is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 20-horse field and, critically, faces no genuine pace rival to press him — Brains, Launch Time, and Desert Of The Sea are prominent types who will sit just off the pace rather than contest the lead. On Good ground over 7f at Leopardstown, Pete's Dream can therefore dictate a controlled, honest gallop without being harassed, which on this track typically produces a race that sets up for horses who can track the pace in the first five or six and then kick. The large field of 20 means midfield runners will face significant traffic through the straight, making a prominent pitch — just behind the leader — the most valuable piece of real estate in this race. This race shape decisively favours the hold-and-prominent horses who can secure a position tracking Pete's Dream in the first four to six lengths, with true hold-up horses facing the highest risk of trouble in running; note that the field contains far more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear, and of the redistributed runners, Micasso and Jazzit are most likely to actually press forward toward their preferred positions given their headgear and recent form.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pete's Dream Controls Tempo
scenarios.trigger: If Pete's Dream bowls along at a comfortable, uncontested pace and the chasing pack settles just behind him through the first half.
scenarios.body: Pete's Dream sets a metronomic gallop with Brains and Launch Time prominent behind him, and the race develops into a sustained test of stamina in the final two furlongs where horses who tracked the pace have first run. Prominent types who avoided traffic and prominent horses with residual finishing speed benefit most here.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Front Oozes Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Pete's Dream goes slower than expected and the tempo is so moderate that stamina becomes irrelevant and positional advantage wins everything.
scenarios.body: A falsely-run race with Pete's Dream trotting through the early fractions means he and his immediate pursuers coast into the straight with a clear advantage while the back half of the field scrambles to close. Horses who are sitting second or third throughout and can quicken off a crawl are the prime beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Strong Pace Plays Into Closers
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent cluster of Brains, Launch Time, and Desert Of The Sea all push forward aggressively and collectively lift the tempo beyond Pete's Dream's comfort zone.
scenarios.body: A pressured gallop stretches the field out and leaves the front brigade vulnerable in the final furlong, theoretically opening a window for the best-handicapped hold-up horse who finds a clear passage. However, most of the field's hold-up horses are redistributed types not truly suited to coming from off a strong pace, which limits the credibility of this shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Traffic Carnage, Wide Runners Thrive
scenarios.trigger: If the 20-runner field bunches at the turn and a significant pocket of horses are blocked, forcing some to switch wide and lose ground.
scenarios.body: Horses drawn widest or with jockeys proactive enough to bypass the traffic chaos inherit clear daylight soonest, and the result reflects positioning rather than pure merit. This is the most chaotic outcome and the hardest to predict from pace data alone, benefiting opportunistic riders and horses with good tactical awareness.

watchPoints.text: Pete's Dream's uncontested lead is the structural cornerstone of this race — watch whether any of the prominent types (Brains, Launch Time) push forward aggressively early and close the gap, as any pressure on the leader transforms the entire pace dynamic.|

With 20 runners on a 7f Leopardstown straight, traffic through the dip and into the final two furlongs is near-certain — watch for horses caught three or four wide with nowhere to go, particularly the redistributed hold-up types forced into unfamiliar midfield positions.|

Suerte ran just three days ago and W J Lee takes the ride — watch the market carefully, as a horse reappearing at such a short interval either has a specific stable intention or carries a significant fitness question that form students should price in.|

Launch Time with Colin Keane is a notable booking upgrade — watch if Keane positions him more prominently than his style tag suggests, as a top jockey stealing a march from just off the pace in a bunched field could prove decisive.|

Gordon Bennett returns from 246 days off for Peter Fahey with Dylan Browne McMonagle in the saddle — the jockey booking is eye-catching given the layoff, and if the market moves it significantly, a well-prepared return should not be dismissed.|

races.name: Renault Ireland Handicap

runners_data.name: Tachos
runners_data.note: Prominent runner from D K Weld (T14:1/13) whose best going form reads 2 wins from 5 on similar ground; the 1m1f trip is a step beyond his recent 8f/9f efforts but his prominent style means he should not be inconvenienced by the crowded midfield.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Tachos nevertheless rates a clear cut above her rivals on our figures, and having run over today's trip and going, she arrives here 21 days fresh and with conditions to suit.

runners_data.name: Sinbad My Dad
runners_data.note: True hold-up type for Seamus Fahey who has shown his best at 10f on good, but only 1 win and 1 place from 15 runs on similar going is a concern; drawn into deep midfield traffic in this shape, he will need everything to go right late.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with a third five starts back his only recent encouragement, Sinbad My Dad returns after 21 days and has run over today's trip; carrying 139 lb from stall 19, he faces a stiff task to break that sequence.

runners_data.name: Bella Colombia
runners_data.note: Consistent mare with a solid placed record on good going (1W3P from 8 similar-going runs) who likes to be held up — in this race she sits closer than ideal but her recent Leopardstown win and two places on good ground suggest she has the tactical speed to adapt.
runners_data.comment: Bella Colombia won last time out and has placed in five of her last six starts, and she has run over today's trip and going before; the 137 lb burden is a stiff ask, however, and a ranking of eighth from 24 suggests she faces a competitive test.

runners_data.name: Quafftide
runners_data.note: Held-up filly without a win or place on similar going (0W0P from 2 GOO starts); the step up to 1m1f from her 7f comfort zone is untested, and 48 days off adds uncertainty despite the straightforward good ground.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts — including two fourths and an unplaced effort — Quafftide is hard to fancy on these figures, ranked 18th of 24, though she has run over today's trip before and draws stall one.

runners_data.name: Guy's Girl
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up performer who will be shuffled into a midfield slot she doesn't naturally want — her best form is over 10f-13f which is beyond this trip, and her chance is tempered by being unable to settle as far back as she ideally needs.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Guy's Girl does at least return after a 30-day break with distance experience to call on, but a third two runs back remains her best recent effort and stall 15 leaves her with plenty to find against 23 rivals.

runners_data.name: Moyassr
runners_data.note: Won at 10f on good (1/10f/GOO) nine days ago for Paul Flynn and comes here in sharp form; a true hold-up type who is crammed into midfield, he will need a good run through but the recent win and quick turnaround are points in his favour.
runners_data.comment: Moyassr landed a win four starts back but has failed to recapture that form since, finishing unplaced last time out just nine days ago; he has run over today's trip and carries 135 lb from stall 23, though a trainer striking at just 4% recently is a concern.

runners_data.name: Pallatine Hills
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who has been off 116 days, an absence that must be respected; his best going form is limited to 1 place on good and the return from a long break in a 25-runner handicap makes this a tough assignment.
runners_data.comment: Pallatine Hills has placed third in recent starts and has run over today's trip, with our rating of 75 marking him out as a leading threat from stall 21 — the main concern is a six-furlong absence of 116 days since he was last seen.

runners_data.name: Star Mind
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type for trainer Gerard O'Leary who has a win from 3 on soft and placed efforts on similar going — the 83-day absence is a query and he will need luck in running from deep in the pack.
runners_data.comment: Star Mind has been only eighth on her latest start and was last seen 83 days ago, making her hard to fancy ranked 17 of 24 on our figures. She does own a win two starts back and has run over today's trip and going, but she carries 135 lb from stall 10.

runners_data.name: Tequila
runners_data.note: Prominent-style runner for Robson De Aguiar who has a placed effort at 10f on good and consistent form around that trip; the prominent tag means he can sit just off the pace and avoids the worst of the midfield congestion.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Tequila does at least bring distance and going experience to this, and 25 days between runs suggests she arrives fresh; carrying 135 lb from stall eight, she'll need to find improvement on recent efforts to make an impact from ninth in the ratings.

runners_data.name: Ohmali
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up type mapped into midfield because the field is top-heavy with closers; Ben Coen takes the ride but the 43-day absence and a record of just 1 place from 10 on similar going tempers enthusiasm regardless of where she settles.
runners_data.comment: Ohmali shaped with promise when second three starts back and has run over today's trip and going, with our rating of 75 suggesting he's better than his official mark of 63 — the risk is that he's been winless in his last five starts and must bounce back from two unplaced runs since.

runners_data.name: Comfort Line
runners_data.note: 9-year-old hold-up performer with headgear (visor) who is actually shunted into midfield in this shape — his recent good-ground placed efforts are his best credential, but racing further forward than ideal at this stage of his career is a question mark.
runners_data.comment: Beaten into sixth last time out and fifth two starts back, Comfort Line has a second three starts back on his CV and has run over today's trip and going before; the 132 lb burden from stall 16 looks the key question.

runners_data.name: Darkdeserthighway
runners_data.note: Hold-up type (blinkers) three days post-last run, which is a very quick turnaround — Dylan Browne McMonagle is an elite booking, but with 0 wins and 0 places on similar going from 7 starts and being pushed out of a natural deep position, conditions are stacked against him.
runners_data.comment: Twice third in recent starts, Darkdeserthighway has run over today's trip and going and our rating has her significantly clear of her official mark — the worry is a return to form after three consecutive disappointing efforts, and she's back out just three days on.

runners_data.name: Jasmine Affanalis
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare who carries 1 win and 4 places from 9 similar-going starts, which is a solid record, but she is squeezed into a midfield position that is not her preference — Luke McAteer will need to find clear running at the right moment.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, with unplaced efforts sandwiched between two runner-up finishes, Jasmine Affanalis looks up against it from stall 20 carrying 132 lb — though she has run over today's trip before and that second last time out offers slim encouragement.

runners_data.name: Sonic Invader
runners_data.note: Front-runner for Noel Meade (T14:4/25 excellent form) ridden by Colin Keane — his history over 14f-16f suggests genuine stamina and the step back to 1m1f should see him travel well within himself; he is a key pace-setter in this race shape.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Sonic Invader does show a pair of thirds in recent form but that seventh last time out is a concern; he has run over today's trip and carries 132 lb from stall 13, leaving him with plenty to prove in a field of 24.

runners_data.name: Tanzanite Diamond
runners_data.note: Hold-up 3-year-old with Adam Caffrey up, sporting a tp (tongue strap/pads) and rated OR=70 — the highest rated runner — with four placed efforts from five on good ground; has shown ability to travel into races and could be competitive if traffic clears.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Tanzanite Diamond at least showed some encouragement with a third three starts back, though a fifth and fourth since suggest he finds winning elusive; experience over today's trip and going helps, but 132 lb from stall 11 is no easy ask.

runners_data.name: Ardeur
runners_data.note: A hold-up filly whose recent form figures (000) are uninspiring and who has finished 14th or 15th in recent Leopardstown handicaps; mapped into midfield out of her natural role, her claims are modest at best.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Ardeur at least has experience of today's trip and going to call upon, and 21 days between runs suggests she arrives fresh; carrying 131 lb from stall two, she holds a small edge over her official mark on our rating but faces a stiff ask to reverse recent form.

runners_data.name: God Knows
runners_data.note: 7-year-old hold-up type who is forced into a midfield berth — his 2nd at 8f on heavy and a placed effort from 15 on good give him some credentials but the overall evidence points to a journeyman in a competitive field.

runners_data.name: Stepdance
runners_data.note: Prominent-style runner for Henry De Bromhead (T14:4/30) who has a strong winning record over 16f-17f hurdles/chase trip — the step back to 1m1f flat is a major reduction in trip and his application of style may suit, but ability to quicken at a sharper pace remains to be seen.
runners_data.comment: Stepdance has won three of her last four starts, but she was last seen 69 days ago and our rating ranks her 22nd of 24. She has run over today's trip, and the ninth last time out is hard to ignore.

runners_data.name: Little Wing
runners_data.note: Held-up filly tagged with a fade-in-finish warning — her three career runs have all ended in 9th or 11th, and the fade profile in a race where closers are already compromised makes her claims very limited.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts, including back-to-back ninths, Little Wing has little in her favour on current form — though she has run over today's trip before and 26 days between runs suggests she arrives fresh.

runners_data.name: Dancing Steve
runners_data.note: Prominent type (visor) who also carries a fade-in-finish flag — his form figures are a string of zeros in recent outings and he has not finished better than 10th in his last five; the style may get him into the race early but the fade flag and form are damning.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Dancing Steve at least has experience of today's trip and going to call on; carrying 128 lb from stall 5, our rating suggests more ability than his official mark of 58 implies, though he'll need to reverse a run of unplaced efforts to figure here.

runners_data.name: Werifesteria
runners_data.note: One of the two key pace-setters for Mrs John Harrington (T14:5/31, very active yard) with Shane Foley booked — a 3-year-old wearing a hood (p) whose three runs have all been at 12f, making this drop to 1m1f a significant trip shortening that may actually allow her to be more competitive with less ground to cover.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts, with finishes of seventh, eighth, and seventh, Werifesteria looks up against it here — ranked last on our figures and carrying 128 lb from stall 14, though 26 days between runs leaves her at least fresh.

runners_data.name: Wild Berries
runners_data.note: True hold-up 3-year-old for Ross O'Sullivan who is funnelled into midfield — her form at 6f-8f on good includes a 14th at Leopardstown and the step up to 1m1f is untested; the style fit discount and limited form on similar going leaves her with a tough task.
runners_data.comment: Yet to score in her last five starts, and a trainer in the depths of a 0/27 run offers little encouragement — though she has run over today's trip before and our rating of 72 suggests she holds some ability beyond her official mark.

runners_data.name: The Holy Apostle
runners_data.note: Hold-up 3-year-old wearing a hood (h) for Brendan Duke (T14:3/6, active) who has been beaten a long way in recent runs — 16th, 11th, and 9th feature in recent form and racing further forward than natural won't paper over those cracks.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, The Holy Apostle has been eighth last time out and ninth two starts back, with little to encourage from recent efforts; he has run over today's trip and returns after 33 days, but a mark of 57 suggests he faces a stiff ask from stall nine.

runners_data.name: Nibras Rainbow
runners_data.note: Prominent-style runner (blinkers) for Paul Flynn (T14:1/22) with a strong recent record of 2 wins and 4 places from 15 similar-going starts including a win at 9f on good — no jockey named which is a minor query, but this is one of the most compelling profiles in the race given the prominent style suits this shape.
runners_data.comment: Ranked a lowly 20th of 24 on our figures and carrying 126 lb for a trainer who has sent out just one winner from 24 runners in the last fortnight, he makes no appeal despite a third last time out and has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Cleopatra's Needle
runners_data.note: Hold-up veteran (hood) who ran 8 days ago — the quick turnaround for an 8-year-old is a flag; 1 win and 5 places on similar going shows she can perform but she is naturally a hold-up type crammed into midfield and the trip is longer than her best form.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts despite a string of placed efforts, Cleopatra's Needle was beaten into ninth last time and faces a stiff task from stall 24 carrying 120 lb; she has run over today's trip and going, but her ranking of 21st of 24 on our figures makes her hard to fancy.

races.paceDynamic: Werifesteria and Sonic Invader are confirmed front-runners who will contest the early lead, ensuring an honest, competitive gallop from the outset over 1m1f on good Leopardstown ground. With two genuine pace horses pushing each other from the gates, the tempo is unlikely to collapse — this should be a race run at a consistent, honest clip rather than a false dawdle that turns into a sprint. The redistribution note is critical here: this field is awash with hold-up horses, and runners like Guy's Girl, Wild Berries, Ohmali, Comfort Line, Darkdeserthighway, Jasmine Affanalis and several others are true closers who will be unable to secure their natural rear positions and will instead be bunched in midfield, creating a compressed, traffic-heavy pack through the middle stages. That dynamic, combined with a genuine early pace, points firmly towards horses who can travel prominently in the slipstream of the leaders — the P-style runners and any hold-up horses with the tactical flexibility to sit closer than usual will be best placed to benefit, while pure deep closers will face a congested highway with limited daylight.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Honest Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Werifesteria and Sonic Invader sustain a genuine contested gallop and the pace holds into the final quarter-mile.
scenarios.body: The front two ensure a true test that gradually exposes the hold-up horses buried in midfield traffic, while prominent-style runners like Tachos, Nibras Rainbow and Tequila can travel fluently just off the pace and strike with a clean run. A genuine gallop at 1m1f on good ground suits accurate pace-stalkers who can quicken from a close-up position.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Outstays Field
scenarios.trigger: If one of Werifesteria or Sonic Invader shakes off the other early and establishes a clear rhythm, rationing their effort across the trip.
scenarios.body: A solo leader setting a controlled honest pace can dictate terms and prove very hard to peg back in a large, congested field where closers must navigate gridlock. Sonic Invader, handled by Colin Keane and trained by Noel Meade who is in sharp form (T14:4/25), has the class and stamina background over longer trips to sustain a prominent gallop.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Chaos, One Threads Through
scenarios.trigger: If the large redistibuted midfield pack creates sustained interference and the winner is a horse who finds a gap late from a slightly deeper position than usual.
scenarios.body: With so many natural hold-up horses crammed into the mid-division, a runner with a sharp turn of foot and a willing jockey who spots the gap can exploit the mess — Bella Colombia has consistent placed form on good going and Tanzanite Diamond has shown the ability to weave through in similar conditions. This scenario is discounted somewhat because many of the horses ideally suited to it are racing out of role and may not reproduce their best.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the two front-runners burn each other out and the gallop collapses in the final two furlongs, gifting late closers a chance.
scenarios.body: This shape requires the natural hold-up types to be in a genuinely clean position to swooop, which the redistribution evidence suggests is unlikely given how many true closers are packed into midfield. Runners like Comfort Line and Moyassr carry some claims if they can find clear air, but this scenario is materially discounted because the horses who would win it are not in their natural positions.

watchPoints.text: Nibras Rainbow has the most compelling profile in this race — prominent style, 2 wins and 4 places on similar good going, recent strong form at 9f-10f, and a trainer (Paul Flynn) who is active; watch to see whether a jockey declaration comes and where this horse is drawn, as it could land in a very favourable spot just off Werifesteria and Sonic Invader.

races.name: Fegentri World Championship (Q.R.) Handicap

runners_data.name: Chutzpal
runners_data.note: A prominent racer with smart placed form over 14f-18f on Good ground at Leopardstown, finishing second over 18f in that going and winning over 14f; de Bromhead yard in reasonable nick (4/30 over 14 days) and the step back to 15f from longer trips looks a fit, 29 days since last run is fine, blinkers on.
runners_data.comment: Chutzpal showed a sharp turn of form with a win four starts back, backed by a second three starts back, and has run over today's trip; the concern is a tendency to disappoint in his most recent two outings, and 170 lb is a stiff weight to overcome.

runners_data.name: Not Just Any Eagle
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who has struggled for consistency (form reading 9-0703) but does own a place over 14f on Good ground and has shown he can stay; amateur rider Mr Cian Murphy on a 7lb claim, but the horse needs things to go right from the back and Leopardstown's flat track at least suits the style.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Not Just Any Eagle nonetheless arrives on a retrieval mission with strong credentials — he has run over today's distance and going, and a third last time out shows he retains ability; the 170 lb burden is the concern.

runners_data.name: Boxing Great
runners_data.note: Stays well — has run over 18f — and won over 16f on Standard, though his Good-ground profile is thin (0 wins, 2 places from 12 runs in similar conditions); a hold-up horse fitted with a tongue-tie, 40 days since last run, and rider Mr P J Cawley carries a 7lb claim, making him an each-way type if the race becomes a pure stamina slog.
runners_data.comment: Boxing Great won four starts back and has experience over today's trip, while his speed rating of 85 suggests he retains more ability than his official mark of 74 implies — the risk is that three modest efforts since that victory leave his current form hard to trust.

runners_data.name: Catalani
runners_data.note: The most likely pace-setter in the race; her recent form (44 in 14f-15f on Good, won over 23f) confirms stamina and willingness to bowl along, and a 17-day turnaround is fresh enough; if she secures a solo lead she becomes a genuine factor, but her last two marks of 4-4-4-9 suggest she may be held by the handicapper.
runners_data.comment: Consistent fourth-place finishes in three of his last four starts highlight Catalani's solid recent profile, and he returns fit at 17 days since his last run, has experience over today's trip, and the 166 lb is the main query.

runners_data.name: Derry Lad
runners_data.note: An 8-year-old hold-up type fitted with a t/p headgear combination (tongue-tie and cheekpieces), who has not troubled the judge recently (form 990555); his Going record in similar conditions (11/15, 0 wins, 1 place) is not encouraging, and trainer T14 of 3/16 is modest — purely a pace-influence at best.
runners_data.comment: Derry Lad has run over today's trip and going, so conditions hold no fears, and our rating edges his official mark — yet he's winless in his last six starts, with a string of fifths and unplaced efforts suggesting he finds a way to do just enough without threatening at the finish.

runners_data.name: Miss Gitana
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner carrying a fade-in-finish flag that is consistent with her 2024 form — she has not won since and has been finishing mid-to-rear despite Good ground form; likely to lead early with Catalani but vulnerable from the turn, and the tongue-tie has not cured the issue.
runners_data.comment: Returned a placing third last time out after a run of disappointments, and has run over today's trip and going before — Miss Gitana arrives fresh on a 14-day break, though she remains winless in her last five starts and carries a hefty 157 lb.

runners_data.name: Peace Walk
runners_data.note: Five-year-old who is a genuine hold-up horse by nature but has been mapped to midfield given the volume of back-of-field types in this field; racing 57 days off a rest, has never won on Good ground (0W0P in sim-going), and any chance requires the front end to collapse; STYLE_FIT of 0.92 tempers expectations significantly.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and 57 days off the track, Peace Walk returns carrying 157 lb with form figures of 7th, 9th and 5th that offer modest encouragement; he has run over today's trip before, and our rating of 69 edges above his official mark, hinting at a fraction of latent potential.

runners_data.name: Makaiah
runners_data.note: A prominent rider who has placed in 5 of 15 similar-going runs and won over 12f on Good; T14 of 1/13 suggests stable is steady, and 45 days off is manageable; has finished 2nd over 12f and 4th over 15f on Good recently — capable of a big run if Chutzpal fails to fire.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked ninth of ten on our figures, Makaiah faces a stiff task here; she has run over today's trip and a second two starts back offers a crumb of encouragement, though 45 days off and 155 lb make it hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: He Who Dares
runners_data.note: Won over 17f on Good and placed over 16f, which speaks to genuine staying ability, but carries a fade-in-finish ⚠ flag and is a true hold-up horse redistributed to midfield due to field composition; STYLE_FIT of 0.90 reflects the positional compromise, and the chance is real only if the pace utterly collapses.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts, with a sixth and eighth also on the card, He Who Dares at least shaped with a little more purpose last time; his distance experience offers some comfort, but at 154 lb off a mark of 60, he faces a stiff task ranked eighth of ten on our figures.

runners_data.name: Supreme Law
runners_data.note: A 7-year-old returning from 364 days off the track — the longest absence in the field — with a form string of 50/00- and zero wins or places in similar going across 15 runs; redistributed from the rear due to hold-up congestion (STYLE_FIT 0.91), and the combination of ring-rust, weak form, and positional mismatch makes this a significant outsider.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and absent for a full year, Supreme Law faces a stiff ask off 147 lb, and his official rating of 40 underlines the size of the task — though our figure of 50 hints at marginally more ability than that mark suggests.

races.paceDynamic: Catalani and Miss Gitana are the two confirmed front-runners in this 1m7f Leopardstown handicap, and with both likely to push forward from the gates, an early contest for the lead is probable, generating an honest and sustained gallop across the full trip on Good ground. Catalani has recent form over marathon trips suggesting she can handle a strong-run race, while Miss Gitana carries a ⚠ fade-in-finish flag that suggests she may set the table for others rather than win from the front. The resulting tempo — two genuine pace-setters pressing each other over 15 furlongs of flat Leopardstown — strongly favours prominent-to-midfield closers who can settle within striking range and produce a measured finish, with pure hold-up types only benefiting if the pace truly burns the front two off; Chutzpal and Makaiah, sitting close enough to the action, are ideally positioned for this shape. The field also contains more true hold-up horses than the map can accommodate at the rear — Peace Walk, He Who Dares, and Supreme Law are genuine back-of-field types forced into a midfield mapping, with Catalani and Miss Gitana the only horses genuinely likely to secure their natural front-running role.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Closers Win
scenarios.trigger: If Catalani and Miss Gitana press each other relentlessly through the middle stages and the fractions are honest enough to drain both by the turn in.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners set up a truly run race and begin to weaken inside the final two furlongs, handing the initiative to horses who settled prominently with cover; Chutzpal, who has shown the ability to finish from a handy position over this sort of trip at Leopardstown, and Makaiah, placed over similar distances in good ground, are the primary beneficiaries of this shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Miss Gitana Fades, Catalani Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Miss Gitana is unable to sustain her effort and drops out early, leaving Catalani alone in front with a soft lead and an uncontested gallop.
scenarios.body: Without a genuine rival pressing her, Catalani controls the fractions, conserves energy, and hits the final two furlongs with reserves intact; horses prominent enough to track her without expending too much early — particularly Chutzpal and Makaiah — remain dangers, but Catalani's recent form over marathon trips on Good ground makes her the key player in this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Grind, Stamina Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is strong but not brutal and the race resolves into a prolonged stamina test through the final quarter-mile.
scenarios.body: Horses with proven staying ability over 1m6f-plus on Good ground find their finest hour as rivals who lack the last furlong begin to fade; Not Just Any Eagle, despite a modest recent record, has placed over 14f on Good and could outgrind weaker stayers if the final gallop suits, while Boxing Great's 18f run hints at raw staying reserves.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the front two burn each other completely and the pace collapses suddenly, leaving a vacuum for the deepest-sitting horses to fill.
scenarios.body: This scenario depends on Peace Walk, He Who Dares, or Supreme Law racing near their natural hold-up position and producing a sweeping late run, but all three are redistributed from the rear of the map and are unlikely to secure their ideal berth in this race shape; the discounted probability reflects that this outcome requires both the fractions to collapse and those horses to overcome unfavourable tactical placement.

watchPoints.text: Catalani and Miss Gitana — if both push hard for the lead from the gates, monitor which one blinks first; the horse that leads comfortably after a mile is the one most dangerous to opponents.
Miss Gitana's fade-in-finish flag is a live concern — if she surrenders the lead before the home turn she becomes a pace puppet that could disrupt the rhythm of horses immediately behind her.

Peace Walk, He Who Dares, and Supreme Law are all true hold-up horses competing for positions they cannot naturally occupy; if these three bunch together in midfield through no fault of their own, traffic problems in the straight are a genuine risk for the horses around them.

Supreme Law — 364 days off the track with zero similar-going wins is an extreme combination; watch in the market for any unusual money as a guide to whether connections believe fitness is there after such a long absence.

Chutzpal's blinkers and De Bromhead's T14 strike rate of 4/30 are worth monitoring in the betting — if the market shortens him significantly, the trainer-jockey combination (Langhard taking the 5lb claim) may be signalling confidence in the fitness and gear change working together.
